reviewer: OMP agent (M16 agent-native factory and migration)
note: FACTORY-008 resume agent work: an agent stops after a partial milestone and the next session reads the handoff, and what it must not do is start over - re-running a destructive setup is how a session destroys the work it was meant to continue. src/factory/handoff.zig makes the handoff a document rather than prose: it names the milestone, the cases already complete with their evidence, the exact next case, and which setups have already run. resumeFrom answers two questions without guessing - which case comes next, and which setups still have to run - so skipping a done setup is the document's decision rather than a habit the next session is trusted to have, and the setups that were skipped are returned as well so a session can log what it did not do. A handoff that points at a case it also lists as complete is refused, because resuming onto finished work is how a session talks itself into redoing it. Running the test found a real leak that the checking allocator caught: the resume duplicates the case name, and deinit did not free it. It also found a language detail worth keeping: resume is a Zig keyword, so the function is resumeFrom. Fault proof: treating every setup as required repeats the destructive setup and the skip assertions fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
